guarantees.claim: When both packer_err and fifo_err are deasserted, error is assigned {valid: 0, code: ErrNone, info: '0}.
When packer_err is asserted, regardless of fifo_err, error is assigned {valid: 1, code: ErrPackerIntegrity, info: ErrInfoW'(flush_st)}.
When packer_err is deasserted and fifo_err is asserted, error is assigned {valid: 1, code: ErrMsgFifoIntegrity, info: ErrInfoW'(flush_st)}.

assumptions.claim: When the EnProtection parameter is 0, the logic driving packer_err must guarantee that packer_err is always 0.
assumptions.risk: A false packer integrity error (ErrPackerIntegrity) will be asserted, potentially disrupting operation.

uncertain_points.claim: When packer_err and fifo_err are simultaneously asserted, fifo_err is silently dropped in favor of packer_err. This may mask a FIFO integrity failure that requires independent logging or recovery.
uncertain_points.risk: Critical FIFO corruption may go unreported, leading to silent data loss or security-relevant misoperation.

uncertain_points.claim: error.info is always driven by flush_st, but the meaning of flush_st during a packer integrity error (ErrPackerIntegrity) is unclear. It may be irrelevant or could leak internal state.
uncertain_points.risk: Diagnostic info may be misleading or, if flush_st contains sensitive data, could be exposed on error path.

uncertain_points.claim: The static cast kmac_pkg::ErrInfoW'(flush_st) may truncate flush_st if its width differs from ErrInfoW; any lost bits could reduce diagnostic value.
uncertain_points.risk: Truncation loses high-order state bits, potentially hiding the root cause of the error.
